source_title: Telco Customer Churn (IBM Sample Data Sets) - dataset page
publisher_issuer: IBM (originating sample dataset, via IBM Watson Analytics sample data sets); widely mirrored on Kaggle
company_context: This is a public benchmark dataset, not a single real company. It models a fictional telecommunications company that provided home phone and internet services to 7,043 customers (described as in California, Q3), used by IBM as a sample for customer-retention analytics. Each row is one customer; the target field 'Churn' indicates whether that customer left in the last month. It is a row-level retention dataset, so the case-level outcome is ambiguous: it documents per-customer churn signals, not a firm-wide trajectory.
business_type: Telecommunications subscription services (home phone and internet) - public benchmark dataset of customer-level records
evidence_summary: The Telco Customer Churn dataset (originating from IBM Sample Data Sets / Watson Analytics, commonly dated 2015) contains 7,043 rows (one per customer) and, in the canonical Kaggle version, 21 columns including the binary target 'Churn'. The overall churn rate is approximately 26.5% (about 26.53% churned vs about 73.46% retained). Fields cover customer demographics (gender, SeniorCitizen, Partner, Dependents), account tenure, service subscriptions (PhoneService, MultipleLines, InternetService, OnlineSecurity, TechSupport, StreamingTV, StreamingMovies, etc.), contract type, billing (PaperlessBilling, PaymentMethod), MonthlyCharges, and TotalCharges; the TotalCharges field has 11 missing values. An expanded IBM version is documented with 33 variables adding geographic and customer-lifetime fields. Because the data is row-level, it supports per-customer retention diagnosis but does not by itself produce a single company outcome.

source_backed_metrics.expanded_ibm_version_variables: 33 variables (demographic, geographic, service, account-level, churn and customer-lifetime fields)
source_backed_metrics.target_field: Churn (binary: customer left within the last month, yes/no)

outcome_evidence: No single firm-level outcome; the dataset documents customer-level churn outcomes (the 'Churn' label) for 7,043 records with an overall churn rate of about 26.5%, intended for building and benchmarking retention/churn-prediction models.
source_limitations: This is a documented public benchmark dataset, not a real company with audited financials; figures are dataset properties, not business results. Column counts vary by version (21 in the canonical Kaggle file; 33 in the expanded IBM version) and the data is fictional/sample by design. Direct WebFetch of the dataset host returned HTTP 403 in this environment; row/column/churn-rate values are corroborated across multiple independent descriptions (Kaggle, IBM documentation references, and academic write-ups).
directly_stated: Canonical version has 21 columns including binary target 'Churn'
Fictional telco providing home phone and internet services; IBM sample dataset (~2015)
inferred: Suitable as a row-level retention benchmark where the firm-level outcome is intentionally undetermined
Contract type, tenure, and service mix fields are the natural drivers for a retention-erosion diagnosis
why_useful_for_opsiq: Provides a documented public dataset for customer_retention_erosion with an intentionally ambiguous firm-level outcome (category 20). Useful for testing OpsIQ on row-level retention diagnosis, for distinguishing per-customer churn risk from a company-wide retention crisis, and as a non-company control that should NOT be force-fit into a single business trajectory. Dataset provenance and fields recorded rather than fabricated company metrics.
